observations.observation: The complete affected-subtree notice, separate domain and asset tables, consent checkbox, inactive confirmation action and wrapped digest remain readable. The narrow viewport shows the initial portion of bounded tables; later columns require horizontal scrolling.

The RTL shell, hierarchy links, title, status, history tabs and restored revision are legible in both themes. Long synthetic names wrap on the phone viewport. The selected tab has a visible underline; dark-mode buttons use the surrounding theme rather than a contrasting native fill.

The complete two-domain cohort, ready-for-review notice, current/projected tuple disclosures, consent and execute controls have a clear visual hierarchy. RTL reverses the layout and table start edge; hashes wrap within the phone card. Some table columns are outside the static narrow viewport.

The committed-evidence notice, export control, actor, timestamp, digest and outcome table are readable. Receipt metadata wraps within the phone viewport. Desktop shows both outcome versions; phone images show only the initial table segment and top rows.

Permission denial uses a generic message without domain contents. Tenant denial shows the generic unavailable-resource message, error code, wrapped correlation reference and refresh action without exposing the requested resource.

The unassigned current placement and independent placement version are clear, with immutable placement history, reason and disclosure controls below. The phone capture includes the current revision and start of the prior revision; further history remains below the viewport.
The blocked-operation notice explains that placements and active children must be removed. Preview tables remain contained, and consent/confirmation are inactive. Phone content fits the page width.
The retained draft/reason, stale-scope problem notice, wrapped reference and refresh/preview controls remain visible and readable. JSON action buttons wrap their text within the phone viewport.

The visual/JSON editor tabs, type key/label, exact parent pin and nested parent picker fit the viewport. The phone search input displays the visible portion of a longer editable value within its own control; no page-wide overflow is visible.

This full-run viewport starts partway through the top application bar while the domain type form and parent picker are visible. The image is a viewport capture, so no claim is made that the entire header or complete authoring form was visually reviewed in this frame.

observationProvenance: Every listed full-run PNG was directly displayed and inspected. The same layout observations as the targeted review were reaffirmed against these new bytes, rather than inferred from matching source alone.

sourceReviewContinuity.qualification: The five already reviewed UI source files retain exactly the targeted hashes. No source edits were made for this archive or review.

preservation.copyMode: Exclusive creation of new archive files; verified SHA-256 equality before/after copying. Originals untouched.
preservation.historicalVisualReview: NOT_RUN_BY_THIS_REVIEWER; non-domain screenshots generated by the full suite are outside this supplement.

otherGates.releaseReadiness: OPEN; the complete governing specification remains the target

limitations: All image observations are limited to the captured 1440×960 and 390×960 domain viewports. This supplement does not add domain inspection at 1280, 1024 or 768 pixels, 200% zoom, enlarged system fonts or physical mobile hardware.

Wide tables remain within bounded containers, but the static narrow screenshots show only initial columns. They do not prove horizontal scrolling, access to every offscreen field, all expanded details or all below-fold content.

Automated axe checks and actual workflow assertions provide bounded browser evidence. They do not replace manual keyboard, screen-reader or assistive-technology review, and no human accessibility approval is asserted.
Arabic RTL layout and visible rendering were inspected; the translation-review-pending banner remains accurate. No professional linguistic or cultural review is asserted.

The full automated execution passes 19 distinct journeys, but this visual supplement inspects only the 26 domain captures. It does not claim visual review of the other journeys or of the 116 preserved historical screenshots.
The reviewer executed no Docker, browser, API, scanner, build or mutation commands. Execution claims come from the preserved root-run report and raw results.
The previous targeted report and all historical failures remain unchanged. This later pass does not relabel earlier failures or close broader product, external-integration, hosted or release gates.
